So just tell me, just give me your full name.
Sure.
I'm Rob Gillette.
I'm the general manager of the Renaissance Austin in the Arboretum District.
I've been the general manager here for 18 years.
We love serving our local neighborhoods like Davenport Ranch and Northwest Hills.
Fabulous neighborhoods.
People love having their gatherings on our Naughty Deck Kitchen and Bar.
Beautiful evening here in October.
And it's a great place to enjoy great food, great wine, beverages, local flavors.
And we have some amazing culinary talented folks here at the Renaissance.
And we love sharing those talents with our local community.
And honored to serve the GREET and STROLE.
Start that sentence over.
Okay.
You were just saying honored to serve.
Yeah.
We're honored to serve the local community.
We absolutely love GREET and STROLE magazines.
Wonderful publications that all these neighbors can enjoy.
And we're just honored to be a part of it.
Amazing.
And tell me a bit.
So the deck out there.
I mean, was that here when you started?
No.
So tell me about what the intention was.
Sure.
How you see it being used now.
Sure.
Yeah.
So the 90 deck kitchen and bar, we operate that as a restaurant bar that just happens to be located in a hotel, not the typical hotel restaurant.
We learned long ago, being someone that went to the University of Texas and having lived here for many years, people enjoy being outdoors.
We sit on almost 10 acres.
The 90 deck is just received finalists for Austin's best outdoor dining patio.
And we're just honored to have this big space.
We spent a million dollars on the deck.
And it allows people to, again, spread out, have room to breathe, look over the beautiful green belt with the backdrop of oak trees, that canopy that's along there.
We also have three fire pits.
It's a wonderful place to go and enjoy company year round.
And it's a very popular spot with our locals and certainly neighbors of the Renaissance Austin.
Wonderful.
Maybe is there anything more you can tell me about working with local communities and people that, businesses that are here?
Because that's what a lot of us are.
Sure.
Sure.
Yeah, we love, as a hotel, we've been named top place to work three consecutive years in Austin by Austin Publication.
And, you know, we really recruit and select our talented ambassadors from the local neighborhoods because we love serving, you know, local businesses.
That is our priority, to serve the local, whether it's small business or larger business.
But we always want to err on the side of promoting local first.
We definitely put a, we definitely have a premium on featuring local products.
So in our Naughty Bar, you'll see all of our draft beers are all local.
Austin or Central Texas beers, distilled products, all of our food that our fabulous chefs create.
They're from local farms.
And we just strongly believe in local.
And the Renaissance brand, really what it reflects is being indigenous to where you are, the neighborhood you're in.
And we take great pride in that.
We love serving our local members, as well as the hotel guests that are traveling here from all over the world.
But weddings, Sunday brunches, a happy hour, we do it all here.
And we particularly love doing it for our local neighbors.
Perfect.
I have one or two more questions about this event in particular.
Yeah.
That'll be good.
So you talked about the food, like locally sourced.
Anything you can tell me about what's out there right now, or this event, like what you guys have put out there?
So these kind of events, they're amazing for networking.
It's all about the relationship, right?
And we know that.
And so when we do an event like this, we could have a flaming mac and cheese.
Our mac and cheese was named Best Mac and Cheese in Austin at the Mac and Cheese Festival.
And so we present those kind of things, or lighter fare like charcuterie with specialty cheeses that are local,
in the goal of having food that tastes wonderful, but it's also conducive to networking and meeting new friends and gathering with old friends.
And so that's what we try to present to these type of local events.
We've been honored to do it before, and we hope we get to continue to do that in the future.
Perfect.
And one last thing, I guess you were out there for a little bit.
I'm not sure how long you were at the event.
Yeah.
Just let me know anything positive you saw about this particular event, people there, what's going on.
I think it's interesting to kind of mingle with the guests that are here.
They always look forward to these gatherings.
And so in our case, some of them have been here before, but many of them have never been to our hotel or they haven't been here in years.
Because our hotel has been a staple in Austin for almost 40 years.
But to visit the nightie deck, to enjoy the indoors and the outdoor flexibility, live music, great food.
Everybody's in the great spirits and happy.
We're in a new month.
We're in the fall, October 1st.
And it always lifts everybody's spirits, I believe.
Perfect.
Thank you, Robert.
Okay.
Thank you.
So basically, just look at me, set up the camera, and just start off telling me your name and your kind of business.
Chad Adams. I've got two businesses, Chad W. Adams Photography and Clara Boya Architecture Photography.
It's kind of loud, so I'm going to put this as close to your mouth as possible.
You can have one more time.
Yeah, Chad Adams, Chad W. Adams Photography and Clara Boya Architecture Photography.
So tell me how you came to be involved with Crete and Stroll.
I was previously involved in another N2 publication in Lost Creek in Westlake.
That one shut down, and I moved to another N2 publication that wasn't as well-run as Northwest Hill seems to be so far.
It's only my second month, so I'm still getting used to the organization.
And then the publisher of the first one introduced me to Mark, and he and I hit it off immediately, and he approached me about advertising.
So tell me about the event we're at now. What do you think of the turnout?
How are these going?
The meet and greet? This is my first meet and greet with the magazine, and it's my second time at Nauti.
I don't think I've ever seen it this full, so I think they've done a really good job of bringing people out.
Perfect.
What have you benefited from so far, like partnering with the magazine? I know it's only been two months, but is there anything that you found that you've benefited from?
Nothing tangible yet, but I feel like I've made quite a few good connections so far already.
I'm looking forward to the next phase of that. What do you call it?
Don't worry about it.
The next phase of onboarding, I guess, is what you could call it, and see where those connections can go.
What do you think did you notice about the people here and the community now that come together?
Everybody seems really ambitious, and that was definitely something that I've found lacking in some of the other networking opportunities that I've had around the Austin area.
You know, networking groups, formal networking groups, informal networking groups.
You know, they all have pluses and minuses, but a lot of them fell short of the professionalism that I was looking for in a network.
And so far, the folks that I've met through Stroll to Northwest Hills has been...
Excuse me. Can I do that again?
It's not called Stroll anymore.
No.
Greet.
The one I used before was Stroll.
My bad.
They have a Stroll.
So I think there's two neighborhoods.
Yeah, I'm with Greet.
Are you only with Greet?
Yeah, I don't know.
I don't know.
The level of professionalism that I've seen with some of the other members of this network is really welcome.
I had some membership in formal networking groups and informal networking groups around Austin before,
and some of them lacked in some key characteristics that I was looking for in folks to network with and, you know, do business together.
And so far, it's been a welcome change with the folks that I've met through Greet Northwest Hills so far.
Do you live in Northwest Hills?
I don't live in Northwest Hills, but I'm a lifelong Austin.
I grew up in Dripping Springs.
My family is three generations Westlake.
So I've been in the Austin area for 40 years now.
What do you think about this kind of group that's very local and sort of neighborhood?
I like it a lot.
I think it kind of harkens back to the days when neighborhoods were much tighter.
It's something that I feel like is missing from my own neighborhood.
You know, I have my core group of neighbors that I know what their daily life is like, what they drive, when their house is empty, when it's not.
Not in a, like, overly intrusive way.
But, like, I like knowing who my friends are and what they're doing and if they're okay.
And a lot of that seems to be lost in some neighborhoods.
And I think that Northwest Hills and where I was hanging out in Lost Creek before, those neighborhoods really embody that sort of kind of old school neighborhood.
Genuine, real neighborhood.
Neighborness is something that's kind of lost in some places.
Okay.
I'd love to give you the chance to talk about your business a little bit to get to know about yourself.
Okay.
Is there maybe something that you do in the part of your work that you feel like makes you different than other photographers?
Yeah.
So, can I do two of them?
Yeah.
Is that cool?
Okay.
So one of my specialties is family photography.
It's taking portraits of children, family photography, family portraits, family lifestyle sorts of things.
And it's really, really fun for me because I have a natural rapport with children.
And for better or for worse, I'm really good with impatient dads who don't really want to take part in the experiments of taking family photos.
So that's where I shine is I have really, really good with kids and really, really good with dads.
And then my other specialty is architectural interior photography.
And my dad was a builder.
My mom laid tile.
I've been an avid DIYer my entire life.
And I love working with designers because they understand color the way that a photographer does.
Builders because they understand proportion the way that a photographer does.
And architects because they understand light the way that a photographer does.
And it's really, really enjoyable to work with folks like that who kind of get my brain and I can get their brain and we can work together to create something beautiful.
Awesome.
That was great.
Thank you very much.
Okay, cool.
So just tell me your name and the line of business that you're in.
Okay.
I'm Adrienne Calhoun and my husband and I own Honeymoon Spirit Lounge just north of West Campus on 34th Street.
Perfect.
Why did you decide to get involved in this group, Northwest Hills?
Yeah, so we moved to Northwest Hills in 2021 and we've been living there for two years and then moved out to remodel.
So we're about to move back to Northwest Hills, but my mom's been in Northwest Hills since 2019.
So we kind of moved a few blocks from her and we love it.
Yeah.
What's, have you been a part of other like networking or business groups?
What's different about one like this that's more neighborhood focused?
Yeah.
Um, I just, I love the idea of meeting other people that, um, Austin's such a big small town.
Um, so I love that there's a community that you can kind of, uh, there's other business owners, but also just great families.
And it feels like you're in a more of a small town neighborhood and we just love it.
And we love the deer running around too.
So, yeah, it's beautiful.
Yeah.
Yeah.
I used to live up on like Spicewood Springs road.
Oh yeah.
Yeah.
I used to live up on like Spicewood Springs road.
Oh yeah.
Near Mesa.
Uh huh.
So much deer around there.
So many deer.
Yeah.
I'm like, it looks like puppies running around everywhere, but we love it.
Tell me about this event right here.
Like what do you think about the turnout and how things are going?
Yeah.
It's fantastic.
Uh, it's such a beautiful space with a beautiful view and we've met a few people and everyone's
really lovely.
So I'm so glad that they put this together and they did a, made a huge effort to kind of
bring everyone together, which is really, really neat to meet other people in the neighborhood.
Yeah.
Tell me more about your restaurant.
I'd love to meet.
They might do this.
North West Hills might put some stuff in the social media about it or the hotel might.
Okay.
Yeah.
Um, my husband and I opened our restaurant and we were supposed to open in 2020 and opened
in 2021 and we were supposed to get married right a few months before opening the restaurant.
Uh, so we were going to call it honeymoon.
It's our forever honeymoon.
Um, all the plans got pushed back.
Uh, we ended up opening in April of 2021, but it's a great date night spot.
It's got like velvet wallpaper.
It's really sexy.
We have an awesome chef that we love and there's a cocktail focus as well.
So we have really unique drinks and, uh, and a cocktails as well.
So it's just a great happy hour, get together and date night spot.
I haven't met any other restaurants.
Yeah.
What makes you guys like, I guess I find it interesting.
The restaurant is like, yeah.
A lot of roofing and contractors and architecture.
What?
Absolutely.
Have you found that interesting or?
Yes.
I mean, um, Reed and I love doing new projects together.
So, uh, it's great to meet other people in construction as well, cause we designed our restaurant ourselves
and might do more in the future, but, uh, it's, it's fun.
We want to provide something that all the people who work really hard and own their own businesses
can come enjoy and be taken care of and return.
So that's, that's why we do it.
Yeah.
Anything else you want to add about your restaurant or?
No, I think we're good.
Thank you so much.
So Hunter, you can just look at me instead of the camera.
Okay.
So first off, just tell me your name and your line of business.
My name is Hunter Malloy.
I'm from Austin.
I've owned a roofing company here for 15 years.
And we're really involved with the community and where we grew up.
And we're kind of thriving and going.
So was that Northwest Hills where you grew up?
I grew up in Northwest Hills.
And so we really kind of started there in the community.
And we're part of other communities around town, high schools and junior highs and all of them.
And trying to stay within the community and, you know.
What do you think?
So it's kind of different having a business group that's very local or neighborhood focused.
Is that what attracted you to it?
Yes.
Yeah.
I think a lot of companies or even roofing companies trying to expand and trying to be everywhere.
Everybody, everywhere.
And we try to be just kind of tight knit and try to keep it with the community and let people know who we are and what we represent.
And we're going to support their kids' events and sports and sponsorships.
And that's what we really try to go for.
And I've seen your logo around and things like that.
And I'm not sure where.
But tell me about, like, what do you guys, like, stand for?
Like, what do you think makes you guys special?
It sounds like you do a lot for the community.
Yeah.
Yeah.
I mean, growing up here in Austin, I work with my sister and my nephew.
I have two best friends.
I mean, we're a tight knit company.
We're really emphasizing, you know, community-based people we already know, referral business.
Majority of our business is referral business, which is, I think that's one of the things that I love most.
Because we're not going out there and picking up random business from advertising and all that.
But it's people that like us, want to use us, and know us.
And that's what we want to be.
We want to be known in the community.
Perfect.
Yeah.
What do you think about this event today?
Oh, this is great.
This is my third or fourth come to in Greek Magazine.
They do a great job.
I met a lot of people.
We partnered up with a few other businesses.
And we send them business.
They send us business.
And it's a great vibe here at Greek Magazine, for sure.
Yeah.
Have you noticed anything else about the people in particular here?
Like, what their attitude or things like that?
Yeah.
I think everyone here, I love talking to business owners because they all get it.
And, you know, they know the stresses and the level.
And you go home, you're still working in your head.
And I think that's what's great about the community of the Greek Magazine because everyone kind of is on each other's side.
And if you can use somebody for your business or they can use you, it's a good networking event as well.
Yeah.
It's been great.
Perfect.
Anything else you want people to know about prosperity?
What else?
I think that's about it.
I guess we've been here 15 years.
We're from Austin.
We love Austin.
We're not going anywhere.
And I think that's one of the things in this line of work of contractors or roofers is who do you trust?
Well, we're here.
And we're always going to be here.
So we have deep roots here.
So that's something I think that should stand apart from many businesses out there because you can start a company like that.
Perfect.
One last question that you make me think of is the hotel.
Like I interviewed the general manager and so they might do some stuff.
Yeah.
Have you been to this hotel before?
Renaissance Hotel?
Yes, I have been here before.
Tell me about the venue.
I've been here a few times growing up here.
We'd come here for small events and things like that.
Never anything professional like this, which I really enjoy.
So we came here a few months ago and I haven't been here in 20 years.
But, you know, it's a great event, great hotel.
But, yeah, a lot of memories come here because we, as children, we come here for one reason or another because our burritums right there.
And so they just kind of travel up here.
So the hotel's been a part of the community?
Oh, yeah, absolutely.
Yeah.
Yeah, it's a great venue.
Perfect.
All right.
Thank you.
Austin, just so you can look at me instead of...
Okay.
So tell me your whole name and what you run in business.
I'm Austin Stone.
I run HRS Window Cleaning and we've been in business since 2013.
We do window cleanings.
We started out doing window cleaning, pressure washing, gutter cleaning, that kind of thing.
Went more so in the window cleaning side of it.
And then we, two years ago, got into window repair.
So we do reglazing, glass repair, storm repair with screens and things like that.
And then we kind of got even further into the storm restoration side and did roofing and
interior damage, that kind of thing too.
So kind of a full scale type of service that we offer for really any home needs.
Perfect.
Yeah.
What do you guys think makes a difference from other companies in the restoration space?
Well, one of the things that sets apart with the window repair side is we're a window
cleaning company as well.
So we'll replace the glass, put a new piece of glass in and then we'll have it professionally
cleaned.
So that sets apart from other window repair companies because they leave it smeary.
They don't know what they're doing cleaning wise.
That, that's what sets us apart on that end.
On the other side, more, more of a family oriented type of business.
I know everybody says that.
We, we, we, I work with a husband and wife team that does roofing and renovations.
They've been doing it since 1997.
And so we, our partnership has been great on the roofing and renovation side.
So that's what really sets us apart is just an established friendly environment.
And have you always lived in Austin?
No, actually I moved here in 2009, married a Texan.
So that's why I'm here.
I'm not leaving now.
But no, I moved here in 2009 and we have two kids and we live in Leander.
We live in Leander.
Yeah.
What do you think about this kind of organization that's neighborhood focused or community focused?
I love it.
I love it.
When Mark just, it was kind of a, he just found me on social media, reached out and we
met up for coffee and it was great because sat down and it's exactly what I was looking
for.
It was advertising and it was also a community focused type of, type of thing.
And it was great.
It was what I wanted.
I wanted the exposure and the magazine.
That's cool.
And stuff like this is also cool too, getting out, talking to people, shaking hands, that
kind of thing.
Awesome.
And what do you think about this event and the people here and how things are?
I just texted my wife and said, wow, this one's swanky.
It is really, really nice.
It's really nice.
I've only been, this is only my second one I've been to and this is really nice.
Great venue, great food, hospitality, nice atmosphere.
It's yeah, it's fantastic.
A lot of really great work went into it.
And so far, how, what do you think about the stroll in Green, Northwest Hills community?
Like what have you noticed about the people here or how they are?
It's not stuffy.
That's what I noticed.
It's for, for, for really the higher end neighborhoods like, like Davenport village and
Northwest Hills.
You don't get that stuffy vibe that you would with like, maybe you assume would happen with
it.
I've never come across that.
But it's one of those things where you might think like, oh, it's, this might be a little,
yeah.
But not, not at all like that.
It's, it's very welcoming.
Everyone's super friendly.
I've never had a bad experience.
That's awesome.
Yeah.
Any value you've already gained from being part of the community?
I don't know how long it's been.
Yeah.
I've made a couple of good connections.
I've been able to get in front of a couple of the bigger companies here, do presentations
for them, let them know what we do.
We've got some good partnerships going right now.
Awesome.
Yeah, I've made a couple of good connections.
I've been able to get in front of a couple of the bigger companies here, do presentations for them, let them know what we do.
We've got some good partnerships going right now.
Awesome.
Anything else you want to say about your business or anything like that?
I don't think so.
I'm just happy to be here.
Awesome.
Thank you, Austin.
Yeah, man.
Appreciate it.
Thanks for coming in front of the camera.
Yeah.
